newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index rises as trade resumes.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index rises as trade resumes.

text.p: The Nigerian share index closed higher on Thursday as trade resumed after a stockbrokers protest over a new transaction fee.
The all-share index closed at 6,559.90 from 6,535 on Wednesday.
At a pre-trade meeting brokers and the stock exchange agreed to defer imposing a new half percent transaction fee until December 1.
West African Portland Cement advanced by 80 kobo to 34.00 naira. Nestle Foods which rose 70 kobo to 32.70 naira.
African Petroleum, National Oil and Unipetrol gained 50 kobo each to close at to 32.60 naira, 33.50 naira and 41.50 naira respectively.
Guinness resumed its slide after a rare appreciation on Wednesday, falling 21 kobo to 8.34 naira.
NAL Merchant Bank dropped 15 kobo to 5.00 naira.
Conglomerates UAC and John Holt were down 20 kobo at 10.20 naira and 11.00 respectively, while Dunlop closed 10 kobo lower at 11.60 naira.
Construction firm G. Cappa went ex-dividend at 7.90 naira, down 30 kobo.
